correctness.rationale: A family with a prescribed pair has S(6,4)=65 members by contracting that pair, and the 21 such families are distinct. The frozen Python search uses the exact shared-pair adjacency; its reverse colour ordering means each remaining prefix inherits a proper colouring with at most the recorded number of colours. Its neighbour intersection and deletion therefore enumerate threshold cliques without duplication or unsound pruning. A separate exact reproduction (/workspace/audit_replay_4.py) generated partitions by peeling off the block of the least remaining point, obtaining 350 partitions, and used include/exclude branching with clique covers of the incompatibility graph. Fixing one anchor in each of the three block-size types suffices by permutation symmetry. There were respectively 6, 4, 3 families of size 65 through the three anchors, all exactly the pair-stars through the anchor, and no family of size 66 in any anchored search. This proves the complete equality statement for the stated finite parameters. The saved C++ output concerns the maximum alone, not its equality classification.

value.rationale: Seven points are singled out by the conjectured boundary for four blocks. At that boundary a sharp proof and the full rigidity statement fill a motivated case not reached by the large-ground-set results, and give an exact benchmark for prospective general arguments. The claim is finite and says nothing about the full conjecture.
